title: Demo tester registry (ops#369)
description: The roster of APPROVED demo testers whose login must survive the nightly demo reset. Written by the approval side on the registry home (registry_home: in servers/live/demo/registry-home.yml) as sites/<site>/demo-testers.json, and staged to the demo box as /var/lib/nwp-demo/<site>/testers-payload.json by `install-box.sh <site> --stage-testers`. IT IS THE SOLE AUTHORITY ON MEMBERSHIP and it carries NO secret: names only. The password hash, mail, uuid, status and roles that actually get preserved are captured on the box from the LIVE database seconds before the wipe, because a password the tester chose themselves exists nowhere else. The reset wrapper reads this file FRESH from disk on every invocation and caches nothing.

version.description: Anything else is CANNOT VERIFY: the wrapper preserves NOTHING and reports the run failed.

generated_utc.description: When the approval side generated this roster. Reported by the wrapper's `status` word; a staged payload older than 48h is flagged STALE (reported, never refused — refusing would turn 'nobody re-staged' into 'every tester lost tonight', which is the wrong direction).

site.description: Advisory only; the wrapper's target is hard-wired [G2].

testers.description: The APPROVED list. Pending join requests must NEVER appear here — they live in the request store the read side never looks at.

account.description: The EXACT Drupal username on the provider half. The only required field. An entry whose account fails this shape is refused, named, and degrades the run — the other entries are still preserved.

approved.description: Optional. If present and false the entry is REFUSED and the run degrades. Belt and braces: the staged roster is by definition the approved list, so this exists only so a write-side bug surfaces loudly instead of a stranger silently acquiring a persistent login.

status.description: Optional. The literal "pending" is refused exactly like approved:false.

x-read-side-behaviour.cache: none — read fresh from disk on every reset
x-read-side-behaviour.fence: an account is only ever touched if uid > 1 AND mail is on @demo.invalid (RFC 6761). The registry says WHO is preserved; the fence says who may be touched at all. Both must hold.
x-read-side-behaviour.not_preserved: everything the tester AUTHORED — nodes, media, feedback, submissions, guild membership and Art.9 consent granted after the seal. That is the feature, not a gap (operator's phase-1 ruling: content temporary, machinery exercised).
x-read-side-behaviour.uuid_is_the_identity: uid is deliberately NOT preserved: after a restore Drupal's uid sequence rewinds to the golden's high-water mark, so yesterday's uid 41 is tomorrow's uid 41 for a different person. The uuid does not rewind, and it is what the ssd half's UID lock (mdl_user.idnumber) is bound to.
collision_rule: same uuid already present after the restore -> UPDATE it (the normal case: the golden brought the tester back and the chosen password is re-applied)

no such uuid but the NAME is taken -> REFUSE that tester and degrade the run; the golden's account wins, because silently overwriting it could hand a tester somebody else's account, including an administrator's
neither -> CREATE, carrying the original uuid so the Moodle-side UID lock still binds

drift.registry names an account that does not: counted `absent`, NOT a failure — a tester approved who has not appeared yet is normal
drift.a real (redeemed) fenced account the reg: ANOMALY — named, counted, and it DEGRADES the run. Under the approval model no unapproved account exists. The seeded `demo_*` (persona) and `nwcdemo_*` (matrix) fixtures are excluded, because nobody approves furniture and a permanently-red check is one an operator learns to ignore.
